quick-2.notes: quick: Fix gh PR-URL parsing in openGitHubPR: gh 2.105.0 prints an 'Event subscriptions are in preview' notice after the PR URL, so taking the last line yields PR #0. Pick the line that parses as a PR URL (number > 0); return ghUnparseable when none does, never a #0 result. Test with the gh notice after the URL as fixture.

findings.text: The description lists a plain 'ok' bullet separate from the pkg.Bar fallback bullet, but the fixture has none. The only ok-status bullet is pkg.Bar, which resolves through the fallback. An exact-match ok bullet (e.g. `Bar` — `x.go:7`) would pin that a directly resolved link stays silent without relying on the fallback.

The Fetch ambiguity also comes from the lastComponent fallback: codex names the methods A.Fetch and B.Fetch, so a bare `Fetch` has no exact match. Removing the fallback would change Fetch as well as pkg.Bar, and both pins still catch it. Ambiguity between two symbols with the same exact name is not exercised.

The parityDoc comment says the tool.py bullet is skipped as an 'unindexed lang', but it has no line number, so Resolve/ResolveAllIn skip it on Line == 0 whether or not codex supports .py. The pin still holds; only the stated reason is off.

The ambiguous `Fetch` bullet also depends on the lastComponent fallback, because codex indexes methods as A.Fetch / B.Fetch. If the fallback is removed it becomes unresolved, so both pins fail on that regression, which supports the test_contract.

The locked decision symbol_shape (no last-component fallback) covers the new spec-fact citation path. This test pins the architecture path keeping its fallback, which is what c-8's parity requirement asks for, so it does not conflict.

planLockFactsGate ignores r.Degraded (internal/cmd/state.go planLockFactsGate): when the symbol index cannot cover the tree, symbols it cannot match are skipped and the gate allows the lock without saying so. The refusal text also leaves the degraded note out. `phase facts` prints that note, so the gate is quieter than the command even though the unresolved lines match.
The parity table compares the gate's lines with `phase facts --json` for all six named cases, and the edge-first subtest checks that no 'unresolved citation' text leaks into the edge refusal.

test_contract line 'if new plan.md instruction rows are missing from the append-only manifest, TestPromptInstructionsConserved fails' does not describe what the test does: conservationProblems (assets/conservation_test.go:208) only checks that rows already in the manifest still appear in the expanded prompt. It never fails on a prompt instruction missing from the manifest. The rows are appended, so they are now conserved, but the contract as written is vacuous. The inline spans `dross phase facts` and `dross prompt partial plan facts` were also not recorded.
By line-length counting, base plan.md is roughly 14.85-14.95 KB, only ~50-150 B under the 15000-byte promptByteCap. The next addition to plan.md will likely need to go into a partial.

_plan.facts.md's field/kind vocabulary (missing/moved/gone/unresolved; 'criteria c-N', 'decisions <key> choice', 'task t-N description') matches internal/facts/facts.go and the factsRow JSON tags in internal/cmd/phase_facts.go.

The new skip branch in check() (facts.go:214) covers anything containCitation accepts that is missing from Tree(), not only gitignored files. A slashed file:line citation into a directory, or into a file inside a nested repo, is now silently Skipped where it used to be reported 'gone'. This is rare and matches the 'unindexed is never reported' rule, but the comment only mentions gitignored files.
check() now runs its own locate() before calling r.Line, so check() can no longer reach Line's len(cands)==0 -> Unresolved arm. That arm stays only for direct callers of Line, as the task intended.
The new test covers a bare-name ignored file, a slashed path into an ignored directory (with both a right and a wrong line), and a genuinely missing file in one table.

notGitTree matches git's English 'not a git repository' text; a localised git therefore errors instead of walking. This is documented as failing closed in /Users/rivil/Development/dross/internal/facts/tree.go.

The new !parsed branch in Resolver.Line also turns a line citation into an unparsable file under testdata/ or fixtures/ into Skipped (it was gone before), even though that file does not mark the index degraded. This matches the task's 'an unindexed file is never reported'.
TestTreeGitErrorClassification covers the not-installed, stderr-not-a-repo, dubious-ownership, broken-index and bare-exit-status cases, so the walk-or-error boundary is pinned on both sides.

internal/codex/codex.go:136 (Symbols): if filepath.Abs fails, the error is dropped and the function carries on with the relative path. Nothing is logged or returned, and Symbol.File comes back relative even though the doc comment promises an absolute path. Add a comment giving the reason (e.g. mirrors Index; Abs fails only when Getwd fails) or return the error.

Symbols sorts by Line with sort.SliceStable, but Index sorts by (File, Line) with the unstable sort.Slice. When two symbols share a line (e.g. `var a, b int`), Index's order is only guaranteed for small slices, where Go happens to use a stable insertion sort. So Symbols(f) == Index([f]).Symbols holds by implementation detail on larger files. The test fixture has no symbols sharing a line.

CanIndex treats every non-Go indexer as ast-grep-backed (type switch on *GoIndexer, otherwise astGrepAvailable). That is true for everything allIndexers registers in languages.go today. A future indexer that doesn't use ast-grep would need this switch updated.
TestIndexKeepsSymbolDataAddingPackage copies the TestGoIndexerExtractsAllKinds source instead of sharing it, so the two fixtures can drift apart. The pinned line numbers match the fixture.

The no-git test only proves Symbols does not surface a git error. Index also swallows recentLog failures, so a git shell-out inside Symbols that ignored its own error would not be caught. That matches the contract's wording; dropping the git call is shown by reading the code, not by a test.

Index now sorts with sort.SliceStable instead of sort.Slice (internal/codex/codex.go:79). This only fixes the order of symbols that share a line, so existing consumers see the same symbol set, now in a fixed order.
Symbols returns nil on an indexer error, while Index still appends any partial symbols. The two are only claimed equal on success, and GoIndexer returns nil on a parse error anyway.

internal/facts/extract.go isPath lowercases the extension (strings.ToLower(path.Ext(base))), so backticked Go symbols whose final component case-folds to a listed extension (`template.HTML`, `template.JS`, `template.CSS`, `math.Mod`) are extracted as path citations instead of symbols and would be reported as missing files under c-1; a case-sensitive extension match would avoid it

internal/facts/tree.go Tree falls back to walkTree on any lsFiles error, not just 'not a git repository' / no git binary; inside a real repo where git refuses to run (e.g. safe.directory dubious ownership) the walk silently includes gitignored files and nested worktrees with nothing surfaced
pathCitation drops a file:line whose line overflows strconv.Atoi or is 0 without comment; rejection as a non-citation is reasonable and x.go:0 is covered by the exclusion test
connector handling for `Sym` (`f:N`) relies on tokenize emitting a standalone '(' prose token between backtick spans; covered by the `Bar` (`foo.go:99`) case

internal/facts/tree.go:559-562: Tree falls back to walkTree on any lsFiles error, not only 'not a git repository' or 'no git binary' as the doc comment says. Inside a repo, a git failure (e.g. a safe.directory dubious-ownership error) silently switches to a walk that includes gitignored files and nested .claude/worktrees copies, with nothing logged.

internal/facts/tree.go fromLsFiles: --cached lists a tracked submodule as a gitlink path with no trailing '/', so a submodule directory ends up in the file list as if it were a file. The '/'-suffix filter only drops untracked embedded repos.

extract_test.go covers every test_contract case: the punctuation table, the exclusion table, commands/flags/keys, symbols with () stripped, spec.toml as a path, paired and bare file:line, the extension set, and pairing a bare capitalised ident. tree_test.go covers gitignore, the nested repo, untracked new.go, and the stubbed and real non-git fallbacks.
isPath compares extensions case-sensitively on purpose, so template.HTML and math.Mod stay symbols. A path like README.MD with an uppercase extension is therefore not extracted.

The Readers list for the phase.Spec.New registry entry (internal/pathfence/fields.go) names internal/facts/facts.go and internal/cmd/phase_mark_new.go, but neither file exists yet; sibling tasks are expected to add them. TestSpecNewIsComparedNeverOpened only checks that the names appear, not that the files exist.

TestSpecNewOmitEmpty checks for the substring "new" anywhere in the saved file. That works for this fixture but would give a false failure if the fixture text ever contained "new"; matching the line prefix `new =` would be tighter.

Silent catch-all on the Kind value set (KindPath, KindLine, KindSymbol, defined at internal/facts/extract.go:13-21). In internal/facts/resolve.go:113, Resolver.Line returns StatusSkipped for KindPath and KindSymbol; in internal/facts/resolve.go:145, Resolver.Symbol returns StatusSkipped for KindPath and KindLine. Skipped is never reported, so a citation sent to the wrong method disappears with no warning. Both methods already return an error; return one for an unexpected Kind. Line's documented unpaired case (KindLine with Symbol "") is fine as is.

In buildTreeIndex (internal/facts/resolve.go, the `continue // unparsable ...` arm), a parse failure is skipped without marking the index Degraded, even when the file is ordinary project source outside testdata/fixtures. Any symbol defined in that file is then reported Unresolved (gone) instead of Skipped. The task does ask for parse errors to be non-fatal, but consider degrading the index when the broken file is not a fixture.

test_contract says 'astGrepAvailableFn stubbed false'. That variable is unexported in codex, so TestDegradedCensus stubs the facts-level canIndex seam for .ts instead. It exercises the same census branch (SupportsFile && !CanIndex).
TestStrictMatchNoLastComponentFallback's T.String case would catch a re-added fallback, because MatchSymbols compares lastComponent(s.Name).

Resolver.Line (internal/facts/resolve.go, the canIndex/index/Classify sequence) looks up idx.byFile[file] for the cited file. When that project file failed to parse, buildTreeIndex skipped it and marked the index degraded, but byFile has no entry for it, so Classify sees zero symbols and reports the paired line citation as Unresolved (gone). A file:line citation into an unparsable non-fixture file should be Skipped, as Symbol does when the index is degraded.

test_contract says the ast-grep census is tested 'with astGrepAvailableFn stubbed false', but TestDegradedCensus stubs the facts-local canIndex seam instead. That variable is unexported in codex, so the substitution is reasonable, but the test never shows that codex.CanIndex really returns false for .ts when ast-grep is missing. It relies on codex's own tests for that.
A broken project source file also degrades the index (TestBrokenProjectFileDegrades). The task record does not ask for this, but it fits c-3's rule that an unmatched symbol must not be called gone.

locate matches a slashed cited path only exactly against the tree list, so a partial path such as architecture/links.go with no internal/ prefix is Unresolved. That is acceptable if checking path existence belongs to a sibling task.

internal/facts/paths.go:317 throws away any lsIgnored error and treats it as no ignored match. The comment's reason (outside git, Tree's fallback walk already listed every file) only holds when Tree itself fell back. If Tree's git listing succeeds but the ignored listing fails, a present gitignored file is silently reported missing. The fallback walk also skips node_modules, so the claim that it lists every file, ignored or not, isn't quite true either.

The taint-regression contract line is proved by TestContainCitationClearsOnlyDeclaredProse, a fixture over copied internal/facts sources, not by the live TestNoDeclaredPathFieldReachesOS. The live gate will only trace this route once a sibling task wires ContainCitation into internal/facts/facts.go.
The Task.Files NotConsumed Readers now names internal/facts/facts.go, which doesn't exist in the tree yet. The task record asks for this, and no test checks that Readers files exist.

internal/facts/facts.go check(): a paired file:line citing a gitignored file passes containCitation (pathfence.Stat for slashed paths, lsIgnored for basenames), but Resolver.Line's locate() searches only Tree(), which excludes ignored files, so it returns StatusUnresolved with fileMissing=false and the citation is reported as "gone" although the file exists

Check overrides kindFor for a line citation whose file is missing and reports "missing" (pinned by TestCheckEndToEnd c-3), while the task record's vocabulary says line → "moved" or "gone"; defensible under c-1, but it departs from the stated mapping and the t-8 payload should account for it
kindFor maps (KindPath, StatusMoved) to "missing" and silently returns "" for (KindSymbol, StatusMoved); neither pair can occur from the current resolver, so this is unreachable rather than a gap

In TestCheckPlannedFilesSuppress the nonexistent files entry (internal/also/missing.go) is also in the known set, so the no-finding assertion would hold even if task files were scanned; the outcome the contract asks for is still asserted

internal/cmd/phase_facts_test.go TestPhaseFactsNeverWrites discards runFacts' error (`_, _, _ = runFacts(t, args...)`) with no adjacent comment. If the command failed early (e.g. FindRoot or the spec load), the hash comparison would pass without facts.Check ever running. Assert err == nil for the clean case and that the unresolved case's error is the 'unresolved citation(s)' one.
factsReport.DegradedWhy holds a file path inside a display string. Filing it in not_paths.txt as a non-path is consistent with how the citation is filed.

Swallowed error: internal/cmd/phase_mark_new.go:141-142, markNewCoversAny drops the error from markNewCitation(f.Citation) with a bare `continue` and no comment. A finding whose citation fails to re-parse is silently treated as not coverable, and the user is told their argument 'is not an unresolved citation', which would be misleading. Add a comment explaining why the discard is safe (Finding.Citation is Extract's canonical Raw and always re-reads as one citation), or return the error.

internal/cmd/phase_mark_new.go markNewEntry: the switch on facts.Kind (defined in internal/facts/extract.go: path, line, symbol) handles symbol only through the default arm returning c.Raw. Today it is correct, but a future Kind would be silently stored as Raw. An explicit `case facts.KindSymbol` plus an erroring default would be safer.

Dedupe compares raw spec.New strings against normalised entries, so a hand-edited entry like './foo.go' would not be seen as already listed. Because facts.Check (via newKey) already treats that entry as covering foo.go, re-marking foo.go is refused as 'not unresolved' instead of reported as 'already new'. It still fails closed.

Passing the same citation twice in one call (e.g. `foo.go` and `(foo.go),`) prints `already new: foo.go` for the second even though the first was only added in this call, and the `already new` line prints before `marked new`. Only the wording is off; behaviour is correct.
The reflowed printFacts doc comment in internal/cmd/phase_facts.go now has one line far longer than the lines around it; cosmetic only.
